No suggestion but thought I'd pass the following tips (from lessons learned the hard way) in no particular order:

  • Start small, very small. So-called MVP.
  • Feature-creep will crush you and your app --period. That's why I don't think asking for desired features this early is a good idea at all.
  • Build for the 80% use case. I know it's hard for devs sometimes to say "forget about the other 20%" but trying to get 100% feature coverage will increase your scope in terms of time and code compexity exponentially.
  • Make the basics fast and easy to use.
  • Have a direction and design philosophy.
  • Be willing to say no to feature requests
  • Design for extensibility (hooks, APIs, etc.).

I tend to get ahead of myself a lot of the time, so I'll indeed first make sure to get the basic app completely functional and up to speed before starting on advanced features. Thanks for the advice!
